# Tree-based structures (Octree, Pointer Tree, Sparse Voxel DAG)

Also called: Sparse Voxel Octrees (SVO), Pointer Trees, DAG-based Voxel Structures

## Overview
Tree-based structures represent sparse volumetric data by recursively subdividing the 3D domain into hierarchical nodes, storing data only for occupied regions to achieve [compression](#4-compression.md) proportional to sparsity [S1, S2, S3]. They solve the memory bottleneck of [dense voxel grids](#1719-voxel-grid-indexing.md) by enabling efficient culling of empty space during rendering or query operations. What sets this family apart from siblings like [Hash Grids](#936-hash-grids.md) (fixed resolution, no hierarchy) and Brick Maps (fixed-size blocks) is the variable depth and branching factor, which allows adaptive resolution and precise spatial locality management [S1, S2, S3].

## Shared principles
All structures in this family share the following mechanism:

1.  **[Recursive Subdivision](#1304-recursive-subdivision.md):** The 3D domain is recursively divided into sub-volumes. In standard octrees, each node has 8 children. In pointer trees, the branching factor $N$ varies ($N^3$ children).
2.  **Sparsity Encoding:** Empty regions are represented by null pointers or absence of children, rather than storing zero-valued voxels. This provides compression proportional to the sparsity of the data.
3.  **[Hierarchical Traversal](#896-hierarchical-traversal.md):** Rendering or access requires traversing from the root to the leaf. This allows skipping large empty volumes (culling) and adapting resolution to view distance or detail requirements.
4.  **Spatial Locality:** Children of a node are spatially contiguous. This locality is often exploited via Morton ordering (Z-order curve) to map 3D coordinates to 1D keys, enabling efficient neighbor lookups and linear array representations in implicit variants [G].
5.  **Subtree Merging:** The core differentiator of the DAG family is the identification of structurally identical subtrees (isomorphic nodes) and their replacement with a single shared instance. This transforms the tree topology into a graph where multiple parents may reference the same child node, eliminating redundancy [S1, S2].

## Subtopics

### [Compact pointer tree](844-compact-pointer-tree.md)
Uses variable branching factor $N$ ($2 \le N \le 6$) and 8-bit relative pointers to compress terabyte-scale [RGBA](#5142-color-packing-rgba.md) data. Choose for interactive rendering of massive volumes on GPU.

### [Sparse Voxel DAGs](2791-sparse-voxel-dags.md)
Merges identical subtrees into shared nodes to reduce memory footprint by 1-3 orders of magnitude compared to SVOs. Choose when geometry has high redundancy/isomorphism.

### [Octree-based structures](2792-octree-based-structures.md)
Standard fixed 8-way branching. Choose for general-purpose sparse volume storage where pointer overhead is acceptable and spatial locality is prioritized over extreme compression.

### [Span Space Tree](4379-span-space-tree.md)
Organizes cells by value ranges (min/max) in 2D span-space rather than spatial coordinates. Choose for [isosurface extraction](#30-isosurface-extraction.md) (Marching Cubes) where value-based culling is more efficient than spatial culling.

### [Sparse Voxel Tree (SVO Tree)](4983-sparse-voxel-tree-svo-tree.md)
Fixed branching factor of 8 with block-based memory pooling. Choose for standard sparse voxel applications requiring fast allocation/deallocation and simple traversal.

### [Tiny LOD](6968-tiny-lod.md)
Constructs LOD trees from splat data with explicit merge filtering. Choose for splat-based rendering requiring hierarchical detail levels.

### [NerfTree](7559-nerftree.md)
Two-level sparse voxel structure for [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md), decoupling coarse geometry caching from fine radiance refinement. Choose for accelerating [Neural Radiance Fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) training/inference.

### [Adaptively Sampled Distance Fields](7773-adaptively-sampled-distance-fields.md)
Compresses SDFs using sign-preserving simplification. Choose for resolution-independent [antialiasing](#4802-antialiasing-aa.md) of complex vector outlines or shapes.

## Background
Tree-based [sparse structures](#5-sparse-structures.md) originated in the early 1990s for efficient storage and rendering of volumetric medical and scientific data [G]. The [Sparse Voxel Octree (SVO)](#8749-sparse-voxel-octree-svo.md) became a standard representation for real-time volume rendering in the 2000s, enabling interactive frame rates for large datasets [S3]. [Sparse Voxel DAGs](#2791-sparse-voxel-dags.md) were introduced later to address the redundancy in SVOs where identical geometric structures are stored multiple times, achieving higher compression ratios [S1, S2]. [Compact Pointer Trees](#844-compact-pointer-tree.md) were developed to handle terabyte-scale datasets on GPUs by optimizing pointer storage and color compression [S1]. These structures are widely used in medical imaging, scientific visualization, and modern neural rendering pipelines [S1, S2, S3].
